1: # Cloud Run Instances as Remote Workstations Guide
2: 
3: This guide documents how to run **Workstation Lite** container images on **Google Cloud Run Instances** (`gcloud alpha run instances`), achieve local-disk I/O performance with persistent Google Cloud Storage backups via the **Hybrid Local-Disk + Background `rsync` Architecture**, connect via SSH or remote IDEs (**VS Code Remote-SSH** and **Zed**), and update the underlying container image.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Overview & Architecture Differences (GKE vs. Cloud Run Instances)
8: 
9: | Feature | GKE Workstation (`StatefulSet`) | Cloud Run Instance (`run instances`) |
10: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
11: | **Compute Model** | Pod scheduled on GKE Autopilot node | Dedicated long-running microVM container |
12: | **Lifecycle** | `kubectl scale --replicas=0 / 1` | `gcloud alpha run instances stop / start / restart` |
13: | **Local Root Disk** | Ephemeral (except mounted PVCs) | **Ephemeral (`tmpfs`/overlay)** — wiped on `stop`, `restart`, or `update` |
14: | **Active `/home/workspace`** | GCE Zonal Persistent Disk (`standard-rwo` PVC, `ext4`) | **Fast Local Container Filesystem** hydrated on startup from `/mnt/gcs-workspace` |
15: | **Persistent Backing Store** | GCE Zonal Persistent Disk (`pd.csi.storage.gke.io`) | **Cloud Storage FUSE** (`type=cloud-storage`) mounted at `/mnt/gcs-workspace` + background `rsync` |
16: | **Incoming SSH Auth** | OpenSSH (`sshd`) or `kubectl exec` | Cloud Run native IAM-authenticated WebSocket tunnel (enabled by default in `gcloud 591.0.0+`) |
17: | **Console Location** | Kubernetes Engine > Workloads | **Cloud Run > Instances** tab (`https://console.cloud.google.com/run/instances`) |
18: 
19: > [!IMPORTANT]
20: > **Cloud Run Console Tab:** Cloud Run Instances are a distinct resource type from Cloud Run *Services* and *Jobs*. They do **not** appear under the default Services list—always check the **Instances** tab in the Cloud Run Console or filter by your deployment region (e.g., `us-east4`).
21:

23: 
24: ## 2. Creating & Managing a Cloud Run Instance
25: 
26: ### Prerequisites
27: Ensure `gcloud` is up to date (`591.0.0+`) and the `alpha` component is installed:
28: ```bash
29: gcloud components update
30: gcloud components install alpha
31: ```
32: 
33: ### Creating an Instance with Hybrid Local-Disk + GCS Persistence
34: Instead of mounting the GCS bucket directly at `/home/workspace` (which suffers from severe object-store latency on small files), mount the GCS bucket at `/mnt/gcs-workspace`. The container automatically hydrates `/home/workspace` onto fast local disk at startup and runs a background S6 `rsync` service (`workspace-sync`) to persist changes back to `/mnt/gcs-workspace`:
35: 
36: ```bash
37: # 1. Create a regional GCS bucket in the same region as the instance for low latency
38: gcloud storage buckets create gs://jasondel-cloudrun10-workstation-workspace \
39:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 \
40:   --location=us-east4 \
41:   --uniform-bucket-level-access
42: 
43: # 2. Create a dedicated, least-privilege Service Account for the workstation
44: gcloud iam service-accounts create ws-vscodium29-sa \
45:   --display-name="Workstation vs-codium29 Service Account" \
46:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
47: 
48: # 3. Grant ONLY object-level read/write access on this specific workspace bucket
49: gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://jasondel-cloudrun10-workstation-workspace \
50:   --member="serviceAccount:ws-vscodium29-sa@jasondel-cloudrun10.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
51:   --role="roles/storage.objectUser" \
52:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
53: 
54: # 4. Create the Cloud Run Instance running as the dedicated Service Account
55: # (Note: SSH is enabled by default in gcloud 591.0.0+; --enable-ssh is no longer needed)
56: gcloud alpha run instances create vs-codium29-instance \
57:   --image=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/jasondel-cloudrun10/workstation-images/user-1-vs-codium30:latest \
58:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 \
59:   --region=us-east4 \
60:   --service-account=ws-vscodium29-sa@jasondel-cloudrun10.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
61:   --port=8000 \
62:   --cpu=4 \
63:   --memory=16Gi \
64:   --set-env-vars="PUID=1000,PGID=1000,REDACTED,WORKSPACE_SYNC_INTERVAL=30" \
65:   --add-volume=name=workspace,type=cloud-storage,bucket=jasondel-cloudrun10-workstation-workspace,mount-options="uid=1000;gid=1000;file-mode=0700;dir-mode=0700;implicit-dirs;stat-cache-max-size-mb=-1;type-cache-max-size-mb=-1;metadata-cache-ttl-secs=120" \
66:   --add-volume-mount=volume=workspace,mount-path=/mnt/gcs-workspace
67: ```
68: 
69: > [!NOTE]
70: > **Regional Capacity:** During Preview/Alpha, some regions (such as `us-central1`) may return `REGION_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`. Deploying the instance in `us-east4` while pulling the container image from Artifact Registry in `us-central1` works seamlessly.
71: 
72: ### Stopping, Starting, and Restarting
73: ```bash
74: # Stop the instance (triggers SIGTERM final rsync flush; stops compute billing; GCS data persists)
75: gcloud alpha run instances stop vs-codium29-instance --region=us-east4 --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 --quiet
76: 
77: # Start a stopped instance (hydrates /home/workspace from /mnt/gcs-workspace on boot)
78: gcloud alpha run instances start vs-codium29-instance --region=us-east4 --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 --quiet
79: 
80: # Restart a running instance
81: gcloud alpha run instances restart vs-codium29-instance --region=us-east4 --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 --quiet
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Security & IAM Hardening Playbook (Isolating the Backing GCS Bucket)
85: 
86: > [!WARNING]
87: > **Never use the Default Compute Engine Service Account (`<project-number>-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com`) for a workstation's backing GCS bucket.**
88: > Because the workspace bucket stores sensitive credentials (`~/.ssh` private keys, git tokens, shell history, and source code), granting bucket access to the default Compute Engine service account means **every** GCE VM, GKE node, Cloud Run service, or Cloud Build job using the default identity in the project can read or overwrite your workspace.
89: 
90: Follow this step-by-step playbook to lock down an existing Cloud Run Instance and its backing GCS bucket to a dedicated, least-privilege identity:
91: 
92: #### Step 1: Audit Current Bucket IAM Policy & Instance Identity
93: Check which principals currently have access to the workspace bucket and which service account the instance is running under:
94: ```bash
95: # Inspect bucket IAM bindings
96: gcloud storage buckets get-iam-policy gs://jasondel-cloudrun10-workstation-workspace \
97:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
98: 
99: # Inspect the Cloud Run Instance's active service account
100: gcloud alpha run instances describe vs-codium29-instance \
101:   --region=us-east4 \
102:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 \
103:   --format="value(spec.serviceAccountName)"
104: ```
105: 
106: #### Step 2: Create a Dedicated Per-Workstation Service Account
107: Create a service account scoped exclusively to this workstation instance:
108: ```bash
109: gcloud iam service-accounts create ws-vscodium29-sa \
110:   --display-name="Workstation vs-codium29 Service Account" \
111:   --description="Dedicated least-privilege identity for Cloud Run Instance vs-codium29-instance" \
112:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
113: ```
114: 
115: #### Step 3: Grant Least-Privilege Bucket & Optional Vertex AI Permissions
116: 1. **Bucket Object Access (`roles/storage.objectUser`):** GCS FUSE only needs to list, read, write, and delete objects inside the bucket. Unlike `roles/storage.admin`, `roles/storage.objectUser` cannot delete the bucket itself or modify bucket IAM policies:
117:    ```bash
118:    gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://jasondel-cloudrun10-workstation-workspace \
119:      --member="serviceAccount:ws-vscodium29-sa@jasondel-cloudrun10.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
120:      --role="roles/storage.objectUser" \
121:      --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
122:    ```
123: 2. **Optional — Vertex AI Access (`roles/aiplatform.user`):** Because `templates/Dockerfile.template` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`, grant `roles/aiplatform.user` on the project if you use Claude Code or Gemini via Application Default Credentials (ADC) inside the container:
124:    ```bash
125:    gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding jasondel-cloudrun10 \
126:      --member="serviceAccount:ws-vscodium29-sa@jasondel-cloudrun10.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
127:      --role="roles/aiplatform.user" \
128:      --condition=None
129:    ```
130: 
131: #### Step 4: Bind the Dedicated Service Account & Enforce IAM Invoker Checks on the Instance
132: Update the Cloud Run Instance to run under the dedicated service account and require Cloud Run IAM authentication on its HTTP port (`8000` for VSCodium Web):
133: ```bash
134: gcloud alpha run instances update vs-codium29-instance \
135:   --service-account=ws-vscodium29-sa@jasondel-cloudrun10.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
136:   --invoker-iam-check \
137:   --region=us-east4 \
138:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
139: ```
140: *(Note: Keep `--invoker-iam-check` enabled so port `8000` is not publicly accessible on the internet. SSH connections via `gcloud alpha run instances ssh` and VS Code / Zed always authenticate via Cloud Run IAM regardless.)*
141: 
142: #### Step 5: Revoke the Default Compute Engine Service Account from the Bucket
143: Once the instance is running with `ws-vscodium29-sa`, remove the shared default Compute Engine service account binding from the workspace bucket:
144: ```bash
145: gcloud storage buckets remove-iam-policy-binding gs://jasondel-cloudrun10-workstation-workspace \
146:   --member="serviceAccount:1076242320305-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" \
147:   --role="roles/storage.admin" \
148:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
149: ```
150: 
151: #### Step 6: Verify the Lockdown
152: 1. Confirm the default Compute Engine SA is no longer listed on the bucket:
153:    ```bash
154:    gcloud storage buckets get-iam-policy gs://jasondel-cloudrun10-workstation-workspace \
155:      --project=jasondel-cloudrun10
156:    ```
157: 2. Check startup logs to confirm GCS FUSE mounted cleanly and hydration succeeded under the new service account:
158:    ```bash
159:    gcloud alpha run instances logs read vs-codium29-instance \
160:      --region=us-east4 \
161:      --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 \
162:      --limit=25
163:    ```
164:    Look for `[workspace-init] Hydration complete.` and `[workspace-sync] Starting background sync daemon`.

168: ## 3. Hybrid Local-Disk + Background `rsync` Storage Architecture
169: 
170: ### Why Direct GCS FUSE on `/home/workspace` Is Too Slow for IDEs & Git
171: Cloud Storage is an immutable object store, not a POSIX block filesystem. When a GCS bucket is mounted directly at `/home/workspace` via Cloud Storage FUSE (`type=cloud-storage`), every `close()` or `fsync()` call must stage and upload the entire object over HTTP to GCS.
172: 
173: Real-world benchmarks on `vs-codium29-instance` (`us-east4`) comparing direct GCS FUSE vs. local container disk:
174: 
175: | Workload | Direct GCS FUSE (`/mnt/gcs-workspace`) | Local Container Disk (`/home/workspace`) | Speedup |
176: | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
177: | **Write 50 small files (`4 KiB` each)** | `12.05s` (~240ms/file) | `0.005s` (~0.1ms/file) | **~2,400x faster** |
178: | **`git status` (medium repo)** | `3.30s` | `0.015s` | **~220x faster** |
179: | **Incremental `rsync` (`--inplace`, warm cache, 1 file changed)** | `0.24s` | — | Near-instant background flush |
180: 
181: ### Why GCS FUSE `cache-dir` (File Cache) Alone Does Not Replace Local Disk
182: The [Cloud Run Instances Cloud Storage volume mounts documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/instances/cloud-storage-volume-mounts) describes an optional `cache-dir=cr-volume:<in-memory-volume>` mount option that caches downloaded objects in an in-memory volume. While useful for read-heavy media/model serving, **`cache-dir` alone cannot replace a local `/home/workspace` for software development** because:
183: 1. **Read-Only Cache (No Write-Back Buffering):** `cache-dir` only accelerates reads. Every file write, save, `git commit`, or `npm install` still flushes synchronously to GCS on `close()`/`fsync()`, incurring ~200ms+ HTTP upload latency per file and ~64 MiB of memory staging per open write stream.
184: 2. **No Per-File POSIX Permissions (`chmod` / `chown`):** GCS FUSE applies uniform mount-wide `file-mode`/`dir-mode` bits; `chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa` is a no-op without custom mount options.
185: 3. **Lack of Native POSIX File Locking & Atomic Rename Semantics:** Tools like Git (`.git/index.lock`), SQLite (`.claude`, `.codex` state databases), and IDE language servers rely on fast atomic renames and POSIX locks. On GCS FUSE, every rename is a server-side `CopyObject` + `DeleteObject` API round-trip.
186: 
187: ### How the Hybrid Architecture Works (`templates/Dockerfile.template`)
188: 
189: ```text
190: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
191: │ Cloud Run Instance Container (16Gi–32Gi RAM, 4–8 vCPU)                     │
192: │                                                                            │
193: │  ┌──────────────────────────────┐    1. Startup Hydration (16x parallel)   │
194: │  │ /home/workspace (Local Disk) │ ◄──────────────────────────────────────┐ │
195: │  │ - Native POSIX perms & locks │                                        │ │
196: │  │ - 0.005s for 50 file writes  │    2. Periodic (30s) + SIGTERM Sync    │ │
197: │  │ - 0.015s git status          │ ─────────────────────────────────────► │ │
198: │  │ - Full node_modules / .venv  │    rsync -rltD --inplace --delete      │ │
199: │  └──────────────────────────────┘    (excludes node_modules, venv, etc.) │ │
200: │                                                                          ▼ │
201: │                                     ┌────────────────────────────────────┐ │
202: │                                     │ /mnt/gcs-workspace (GCS FUSE)      │ │
203: │                                     │ gs://...-workstation-workspace     │ │
204: │                                     │ stat/type cache: -1 (unlimited)    │ │
205: │                                     │ metadata-cache-ttl-secs: 120       │ │
206: │                                     └────────────────────────────────────┘ │
207: └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
208: ```
209: 
210: 1. **Startup Hydration (`/custom-cont-init.d/99-setup-user`):**
211:    * Runs synchronously during S6 container initialization (`init-custom-files`), before `svc-vscodium-web` or `custom-svc-workspace-sync` starts.
212:    * Detects if `/mnt/gcs-workspace` is mounted in `/proc/mounts` and `/home/workspace` is not a volume mount. (If running on GKE where `/mnt/gcs-workspace` is not mounted, hydration and background sync are automatically no-ops.)
213:    * Uses 16 parallel `rsync` workers (`find /mnt/gcs-workspace -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print0 | xargs -0 -r -P 16 -I {} rsync -a ... "{}" /home/workspace/`) with `set -o pipefail` to saturate GCS FUSE read concurrency, hydrating ~1 GiB / 6,500+ files in ~35–75 seconds instead of 5+ minutes with single-threaded `rsync`.
214:    * Only if the parallel hydration pipeline exits with status `0` does it record the initial local file manifest (`/run/workspace-sync/manifest`) and write the `/run/workspace-hydrated` sentinel file. The sync daemon refuses to run unless `/run/workspace-hydrated` exists, preventing an unhydrated or partially hydrated `/home/workspace` from ever wiping the bucket.
215:    * Sets ownership (`chown -R abc:abc /home/workspace`) and enforces true POSIX permissions on `/home/workspace/.ssh` (`chmod 700 ~/.ssh`, `chmod 600` on private keys, `chmod 644` on `.pub`, `known_hosts`, and `config`).
216: 2. **Periodic & Graceful-Shutdown Incremental Sync (`/custom-services.d/workspace-sync` & `/usr/local/bin/workspace-sync-now`):**
217:    * Supervised by S6 Overlay v3 as `custom-svc-workspace-sync` with `ENV S6_SERVICES_GRACETIME=8000` (giving S6 services an 8-second shutdown grace period within Cloud Run's 10-second `SIGTERM` window instead of S6's default 3-second timeout).
218:    * Runs `/usr/local/bin/workspace-sync-now` every `WORKSPACE_SYNC_INTERVAL` seconds (default `30s`) and traps `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, and `SIGHUP` to perform a final blocking sync (`workspace-sync-now --wait`) when the instance stops or restarts.
219:    * Uses `flock` on `/run/workspace-sync/lock` (inside a mode `0777` `/run/workspace-sync` directory with `umask 000` so both `root` and `abc` can invoke it) to prevent overlapping sync runs, and ignores `rsync` exit code `24` (vanished temporary files during active builds).
220:    * You can also trigger an immediate sync manually at any time (as either `abc` or `root`) by running:
221:      ```bash
222:      workspace-sync-now --wait
223:      # Or force a full destination directory walk with rsync --delete:
224:      workspace-sync-now --wait --full-delete
225:      ```
226: 3. **Why Local Manifest Deletion Tracking + 16x Parallel `rsync -rltDO --inplace --no-perms --no-owner --no-group` Is Used:**
227:    * **Avoiding Temp-File Rename Overhead (`--inplace`):** Standard `rsync -a` writes every updated file to a temporary `.filename.XXXXXX` object and then renames it over `filename`. On GCS FUSE, a `rename()` triggers a server-side GCS `CopyObject` + `DeleteObject`, doubling the API requests and write latency (`2.61s` vs `1.26s` for 10 files). Passing `--inplace` writes directly to the target object in a single `close()`/upload.
228:    * **Avoiding GCS FUSE `readdir()` Scans via Local Manifest Diffing (`1.3s` vs `42.8s`):** In GCS FUSE, `stat-cache` and `type-cache` only cache `lstat()` (`LookUpInode`/`GetInodeAttributes`), *not* directory listings (`readdir()` / `Objects: list`). Running a single-threaded `rsync --delete` forces `rsync` to call `readdir()` on all ~1,400 directories in `/mnt/gcs-workspace` sequentially (~30ms HTTP call per directory = **42.8 seconds** per sync!). Instead, `workspace-sync-now` scans local `/home/workspace` in **~50ms** (`cd /home/workspace && find . ... -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z`), diffs against the previous manifest (`/run/workspace-sync/manifest`) with `LC_ALL=C comm -z -23` to unlink any locally deleted files/directories directly on `/mnt/gcs-workspace`, and runs 16 parallel `rsync -rltDO --inplace` workers that hit GCS FUSE's in-memory `stat-cache` in **~1.3 seconds** total.
229:    * **Skipping Redundant FUSE Metadata Calls (`-O --no-perms --no-owner --no-group`):** Because `/mnt/gcs-workspace` is mounted with `uid=1000;gid=1000;file-mode=0700;dir-mode=0700`, skipping redundant `chown`/`chmod` and directory mtime (`-O`) syscalls on FUSE avoids unnecessary metadata round-trips while preserving file modification timestamps (`-t`) and symlinks (`-l`).
230:    * **Exclusions:** Heavy regenerable directories (`node_modules`, `venv`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.cache`, `.gemini`, `.npm`, `.tmp`, `lost+found`) stay strictly on fast local disk and are excluded from GCS sync.
231: 
232: ### Recommended GCS FUSE `mount-options` for `/mnt/gcs-workspace`
233: Based on the [official Cloud Run Instances GCS Volume Mount documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/instances/cloud-storage-volume-mounts):
234: 
235: ```text
236: mount-options="uid=1000;gid=1000;file-mode=0700;dir-mode=0700;implicit-dirs;stat-cache-max-size-mb=-1;type-cache-max-size-mb=-1;metadata-cache-ttl-secs=120"
237: ```
238: *(Note: Use semicolons `;` in `gcloud alpha run instances` CLI flags, or commas `,` in YAML `mountOptions`.)*
239: 
240: * `uid=1000;gid=1000`: Mounts the volume owned by `abc:abc` (`1000:1000` when `PUID=1000,PGID=1000` is set). By default, Cloud Run mounts GCS volumes as `root:root` (`0:0`), and `chown -R` on GCS FUSE is a no-op.
241: * `file-mode=0700;dir-mode=0700`: Preserves executable bits (`+x`) on scripts and CLI binaries in `.local/bin` (such as `claude`) across container restarts.
242: * `implicit-dirs`: Ensures GCS FUSE recognizes directories created by external tools (`gcloud storage cp/rsync`) that lack explicit directory placeholder objects.
243: * `stat-cache-max-size-mb=-1;type-cache-max-size-mb=-1`: Allows GCS FUSE's in-memory stat and type caches to grow as needed without evicting entries when workspaces exceed 20,000 files (~1,500 bytes/file for stat cache, ~200 bytes/file for type cache).
244: * `metadata-cache-ttl-secs=120`: Keeps file/directory metadata cached in memory for 120 seconds (longer than the 30-second `rsync` interval), so periodic `rsync` scans hit RAM instead of issuing GCS `Objects: list`/`stat` calls.
245: 
246: ### Memory Accounting & Git Repository Maintenance
247: * **Container Memory Accounting:** In Cloud Run Instances, the container's writable local filesystem (`/home/workspace` on root overlay/`tmpfs`), GCS FUSE's in-memory metadata caches, and GCS FUSE write staging buffers (~64 MiB per open write stream) **all count toward the container's memory limit** (up to `32 GiB` max). Provision at least `16Gi`–`32Gi` of memory (`--memory=16Gi` or `--memory=32Gi`).
248: * **Keep `.git` Repositories Packed (`git gc`):** A repository with thousands of loose `.git/objects/xx/...` files creates thousands of separate GCS objects. Running `git gc` inside large repositories packs thousands of loose objects into a single `.pack` + `.idx` file pair (e.g., reducing `cycling-coach/.git` from `6,339` objects to `220` files), dramatically speeding up both startup hydration and background `rsync`.

252: ## 4. Connecting via Terminal SSH, VS Code Remote-SSH, and Zed IDE
253: 
254: ### A. Terminal SSH
255: To open an interactive shell directly from your terminal:
256: ```bash
257: gcloud alpha run instances ssh vs-codium29-instance \
258:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 \
259:   --region=us-east4
260: ```
261: *(Note: The Cloud Run SSH tunnel logs you into the container as `root`. To switch to the standard workstation user `abc` with Oh My Zsh, run `su - abc`.)*
262: 
263: ### B. Configuring `~/.ssh/config` for Remote IDEs (VS Code & Zed)
264: Under the hood, `gcloud alpha run instances ssh` generates a short-lived SSH certificate (`~/.ssh/google_compute_engine_cert/<project>_<region>_instance_<name>-cert.pub`), establishes an IAM-authenticated WebSocket tunnel (`gcloud alpha run start-iap-tunnel`), and connects standard OpenSSH over that tunnel.
265: 
266: First, run the CLI SSH command once so `gcloud` generates your Google Compute Engine SSH keypair (`~/.ssh/google_compute_engine`) and certificate (`~/.ssh/google_compute_engine_cert/...`):
267: ```bash
268: printf "exit\n" | gcloud alpha run instances ssh vs-codium29-instance \
269:   --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 \
270:   --region=us-east4
271: ```
272: 
273: Then add the following verified host entry to your local `~/.ssh/config`:
274: ```sshconfig
275: Host cloudrun-workstation
276:     HostName cloud-run-default
277:     User root
278:     IdentityFile ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine
279:     CertificateFile ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine_cert/jasondel-cloudrun10_us-east4_instance_vs-codium29-instance-cert.pub
280:     IdentitiesOnly yes
281:     CheckHostIP no
282:     HashKnownHosts no
283:     HostKeyAlias cloud-run-default
284:     StrictHostKeyChecking no
285:     UserKnownHostsFile ~/.ssh/google_compute_known_hosts
286:     ProxyUseFdpass no
287:     ProxyCommand gcloud alpha run start-iap-tunnel --project_number=1076242320305 --project_id=jasondel-cloudrun10 --workload_type=instance --deployment_name=vs-codium29-instance --region=us-east4 --iap-tunnel-url-override=wss://us-east4.ssh.run.app/v4
288: ```
289: *(Tip: If the short-lived SSH certificate expires later, simply run `gcloud alpha run instances ssh vs-codium29-instance --project=jasondel-cloudrun10 --region=us-east4` once to refresh it.)*
290: 
291: ### C. Connecting with VS Code Remote-SSH
292: 1. Install the **Remote - SSH** extension (`ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh`) in VS Code.
293: 2. Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P`) -> **Remote-SSH: Connect to Host...**
294: 3. Select **`cloudrun-workstation`**.
295: 4. Open folder `/home/workspace`.
296: 
297: ### D. Connecting with Zed IDE
298: Zed natively uses your system OpenSSH configuration and `ProxyCommand`:

347: ### A. `ERROR: (gcloud.alpha.run.start-iap-tunnel) Error while connecting [4003: 'failed to connect to backend'] (Failed to connect to port 22)`
348: * **Cause:** Cloud Run's SSH proxy (`wss://<region>.ssh.run.app`) rejects tunnel connections until the container finishes S6 initialization (`99-setup-user`) and binds its readiness port (`8000`). 352: * **Cause:** Stopped Cloud Run Instances created under older Alpha/Preview backend revisions can occasionally fail in Cloud Run's control plane when resuming cached container resources after backend rollouts.
